policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'nor yet be troubled' renders either negative conjunction identically; no note is mapped here and nothing in the English distinguishes μηδέ from μήτε.
ASV reads 'the day of the Lord', rendering κυρίου; Χριστοῦ would have produced 'the day of Christ'.
ASV text reads 'the man of sin' (ἁμαρτίας) and relegates ἀνομίας to the margin: the mapped textual_variant note says 'Many ancient authorities read lawlessness.'
ASV renders one 'as God', attached to the showing-forth clause ('setting himself forth as God'); the sitting clause is simply 'he sitteth in the temple of God', with no rendering of an added ὡς θεόν.
ASV 'in his own season' renders the reflexive ἑαυτοῦ; plain αὐτοῦ would give 'in his season'.
ASV text reads 'the Lord Jesus', with the mapped textual_variant note 'Some ancient authorities omit Jesus' marking the omission as the margin.
ASV text reads 'shall slay' (ἀνελεῖ); the mapped textual_variant note 'Some ancient authorities read consume' puts ἀναλώσει in the margin.
ASV 'for them that perish' renders the bare dative τοῖς ἀπολλυμένοις; the RP reading's ἐν would have given 'in them that perish'.
ASV 'God sendeth them a working of error' is present tense, rendering πέμπει; πέμψει would give 'shall send'.
πάντες and ἅπαντες are both rendered 'all'; the orthographic variant leaves no trace in the English and no note is mapped here.
ASV 'had pleasure in unrighteousness' renders εὐδοκήσαντες with its dative complement; the English 'in' belongs to the verb's idiom and does not show whether ἐν stood in the Greek.
ASV text reads 'chose you from the beginning' (ἀπ᾽ ἀρχῆς); the mapped textual_variant note 'Many ancient authorities read as firstfruits' places ἀπαρχήν in the margin.
ASV 'whereunto he called you' has no 'also', but ASV routinely leaves ascensive καί untranslated, so its absence does not exclude the reading; no note is mapped here.
ASV 'and God our Father' cannot show whether the Greek article stood before θεός; English supplies no article either way.
ASV reads 'God our Father', apposition rendering θεὸς ὁ πατὴρ ἡμῶν; the RP καί would have produced 'God and our Father'.
ASV 'comfort your hearts and establish them' gives στηρίξαι the same object as παρακαλέσαι ('them' = your hearts); an added ὑμᾶς would have produced 'establish you'.
ASV 'in every good work and word' preserves the order ἔργῳ καὶ λόγῳ; the RP reading would give 'word and work'.
